title: init seeds an Elixir decision tree into every project and Destination cannot decline it
body:
`intent init` writes an Elixir/Phoenix decision tree into every project regardless of declared language, and `Destination` has no form that can express declining it.

**DRIVEN, NOT READ.** `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/embedded_init.rs` runs `init offline` in a bare tempdir -- no language declared -- and asserts `intent/llm/DECISION_TREE.md` is written and non-empty. That test passes, so the behaviour is established by an existing committed drive rather than by reading the seeding table.

**THE TABLE.** `intentsvcs::init::DESTINATIONS` maps `llm/_DECISION_TREE.md` to `At("intent/llm/DECISION_TREE.md")`. `Destination` has exactly two variants -- `At` and `NotByInit` -- so there is no per-language disposition to reach for. The content is Elixir/Phoenix-specific: the template's own first section heading is `## Elixir/Phoenix Decision Tree`.

**WHY THIS IS NOT A DOC BUG.** It was FOUND as one. `in-standards/SKILL.md` told every session at boot that the file was `laid down by intent lang init elixir`, in the sentence after one saying `intent init` creates it not at all. Both were false, they were false consistently with each other, and the skill's version described a DEFENSIBLE design -- a per-language artefact laid down by the per-language verb. **The prose was not describing the code wrongly so much as describing a better design that was never built**, which is why a reader had no reason to doubt it. The prose is corrected separately; this is the thing underneath.

**THE COST IS NOT NOISE, IT IS A FALSE SIGNAL ABOUT PROVENANCE.** A Rust or Swift project contains a file that looks chosen and was not. Any reader -- human or agent -- that treats presence as evidence of a decision reads Elixir placement guidance as this project's ruling on where code goes. `in-standards` step 1 instructed exactly that reading until today.

**RELATION TO THE LLM-CONFIG PROGRAMME.** This is the programme's own class arriving in the seeding table: an artefact whose writer, whose population and whose applicability disagree, with nothing binding them. It is filed as its own defect rather than folded into the programme because it is true and costly independently of whether the programme is ever built.

**NOT CLAIMED.** That the right answer is `lang init elixir` -- that is the design question and it is open. Possible dispositions include a per-language variant on `Destination`, moving the template to the elixir language pack, or dropping the artefact as MODULES.md was dropped on 2026-08-24 for a related reason. Also not claimed: how many estates currently carry an unwanted copy; nobody has counted.



## AMENDED 2026-09-09 BY ic, FROM ST0065/WP-01's REVIEW OF THE BOOTSTRAP SET -- TWO THINGS, AND THE FIRST CHANGES THE REMEDY'S SIZE

### A FOURTH DISPOSITION EXISTS, IT IS ALREADY IN USE, AND IT NEEDS NO CHANGE TO `Destination`

This filing says *`Destination` has no form that can express declining it*, and lists three possible dispositions: a per-language variant on `Destination`, moving the template to the elixir language pack, or dropping the artefact. **All three are changes to a MECHANISM. A fourth needs none.**

**The template engine already has language conditionals and `_AGENTS.md` already uses them across five languages.** Driven: `rootfiles.rs:293-298` parses `[[#lang <name>]]` and `[[#nolang]]`; `lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md` carries `[[#lang elixir]]`, `[[#lang rust]]`, `[[#lang swift]]`, `[[#lang lua]]`, `[[#lang shell]]` and `[[#nolang]]`. **`_DECISION_TREE.md` carries ZERO of them, and it is the ONLY seeded `llm/` template that is language-specific at all.**

Measured across the three templates `init` actually seeds under `llm/`:

| template | lines | Elixir/Phoenix markers | `[[#` conditionals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_DECISION_TREE.md` | 80 | 13 | **0** |
| `_RULES.md` | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| `_ARCHITECTURE.md` | 9 | 0 | 0 |

**THE CONTRAST IS THE FINDING, NOT THE COUNT.** `init.rs`'s own comment records that `_RULES` and `_ARCHITECTURE` were **rewritten rather than carried over** from v2, because the v2 pair was *an incomplete template that reads like a spec*, and that both now *say what belongs in them, say that they are empty ON PURPOSE, and stop*. **The same review rewrote two of the three and left the third**, and the third is the one carrying 80 lines of another language's placement advice. Nothing recorded a decision to leave it.

So the disposition set should include: **wrap the body in `[[#lang elixir]]` with a `[[#nolang]]` alternative saying the project has not declared a language.** It costs no new variant, no move between packs, and no loss of the artefact for the projects it fits.

### THE SEEDED FILE POINTS THREE TIMES AT A FILE THE SAME TABLE DELIBERATELY REFUSES TO SEED

**This half is independent of the language question and survives every disposition above except dropping the artefact.** `_DECISION_TREE.md` instructs its reader to consult `MODULES.md` three times:

- line 4: *Always cross-reference MODULES.md -- if a module already owns that concern, put the code there.*
- line 47: *Check MODULES.md*
- line 49: *If no: register in MODULES.md first, then create the module*

**`DESTINATIONS` refuses to seed `MODULES.md`, twenty-six lines from the entry that seeds this file**, with the fullest reason in the table: *a hand-maintained index of a tree the store already indexes*, hv's ruling of 2026-08-24, measured at ~354KB over ~367 rows.

**SO A FRESH ELIXIR PROJECT -- the case where this template's CONTENT is correct -- still gets a file that opens by telling the reader to always cross-reference something that does not exist and that this tool has deliberately decided not to create.** The Highlander ruling that retired `MODULES.md` reached the seeding table and did not reach the seeded prose. **Two entries in one `const`, both right on their own terms, composing into an instruction nobody can follow** -- which is the same shape this filing already identifies one level up, where two correct local decisions compose into a wrong global outcome.

### NOT CLAIMED

Whether the `[[#lang]]` route is the RIGHT disposition -- that remains the open design question this filing names, and hv's or the pen's to settle. Only that it belongs on the list, and that its cost is different in kind from the three already there. Also not counted: how many other seeded or synced templates still cite `MODULES.md`; only the four `llm/` and `prj/` templates in the seeding set were checked, and `_DECISION_TREE.md` is the only one that cites it.

---

**AMENDMENT (ic, 2026-09-09, on vc's ruling): THE UNCOUNTED POPULATION IS COUNTED, AND THE COUNT IS THE WRONG ANSWER.**

This filing closes with *"also not counted: how many other seeded or synced templates still cite `MODULES.md`; only the four `llm/` and `prj/` templates in the seeding set were checked, and `_DECISION_TREE.md` is the only one that cites it."* **Counted: EIGHT of 65 files under `lib/templates/`. But the number is not the finding, because THREE of the eight are correct, and recording "8" would flatten exactly the distinction that matters.**

**GUARDED -- each of these carries hv's 2026-08-24 retirement ruling properly, and one of them is right BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by wording:**

- `llm/_CLAUDE.md:21` -- *"OPTIONAL Highlander registry. `intent init` does not create one ... its absence is the normal case and is not a gap to fix."*
- `prime/operational-knowledge.md:41` -- *"Where the project keeps an `intent/llm/MODULES.md` registry ..."*
- `hooks/module_check_hook.json:9` -- guards on `if [ -f intent/llm/MODULES.md ]`, so on a project without the registry it short-circuits and says nothing. **This one cannot become wrong through rewording, which is a stronger kind of correct than the other two.**

**UNCONDITIONAL -- instructing a reader to consult a file `init` deliberately refuses to create:** `llm/_DECISION_TREE.md` (x3), `archetypes/elixir/ash_resource.ex.eex:5`, `archetypes/elixir/service.ex.eex:6`, `llm/_AGENTS.md:252` (a file-map row asserting it as standard layout), `llm/_ARCHETYPES.md:26` (documents the archetype reminders as intended behaviour, which certifies the defect rather than committing it).

**REACH DRIVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because a wrong template that never lands is not a defect.** `_DECISION_TREE.md` is `At(...)` -- **every project, at `init`**. `_AGENTS.md` arrives via `intent agents sync` and is **live in this repo at `AGENTS.md:192`**. `_ARCHETYPES.md` and both `.eex` arrive via `intent lang init`. **All five land somewhere; none is dead template.**

**AND THIS FILING'S OWN CLAIM NEEDS CORRECTING, IN THE REGISTER IT DESERVES: LITERALLY WRONG, SUBSTANTIVELY RIGHT.** `_CLAUDE.md` cites `MODULES.md` too, inside the very seeding set this filing says it checked -- so *"`_DECISION_TREE.md` is the only one that cites it"* is false as written. **It is true of the only thing that matters: `_DECISION_TREE.md` is the only UNCONDITIONAL citer in that set.** What this filing was owed was the discriminator, not a bigger number.

**THE DURABLE HALF IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE CENSUS: A RULING PROPAGATES ALONG THE PATH OF ATTENTION, AND GENERATED-FROM ARTEFACTS ARE OFF IT.** hv's ruling reached **3 of 8** homes, and the three it reached are the ones a human re-reads -- `CLAUDE.md`, a prime doc, and a hook. **The five it missed are an Elixir decision tree, two `.eex` comment blocks, a file-map line and a doc ABOUT templates** -- documents people generate FROM rather than read. That predicts where to look next for any ruling's unpropagated remainder, and it is the general form of the same failure the estate met four separate times on 2026-09-09.

**NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: none of the five is corrected.** Four are one-line edits and the fifth is `_DECISION_TREE.md`, which this filing already says needs a design ruling. **Quietly fixing the other four would leave that ruling looking smaller than it is** (vc, 2026-09-09). Cross-reference: the full working is catalogued at `ST0065`'s `_catalogue-wp01.md`, finding 2 and section 9.
